title: Living Soils
summary: Comprenez la vie biologique du sol (vers, champignons, bactéries, humus) et comment le système des planches permanentes nourrit naturellement vos cultures.

pages.title: The role of mulching
pages.text:
Mulching in the walkways is essential :

It retains water like a sponge, keeping the soil moist.

It slows down the flow of water during heavy rain, which limits erosion.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle du paillage

Microorganisms (bacteria and filamentous fungi) feed on the mulch.

pages.title: The role of micro-organisms and
pages.text:
insects

They become food for woodlice, insects (termites, spiders, millipedes...) and earthworms.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle des micro-organismes et

pages.title: The role of micro-organisms and
pages.text:
insects

All these organisms participate in the decomposition of the mulch into compost. We can thus speak of surface

compost in the walkways. The excrements and corpses of microorganisms and insects decompose and in turn

nourish the compost.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle des micro-organismes et

pages.title: The role of micro-organisms and
pages.text:
insects

By digging tunnels, earthworms and termites also facilitate the circulation of air and water and help the roots of

plants find their way.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle des micro-organismes et

pages.title: The role of micro-organisms and
pages.text:
insects

The decomposition of organic matter releases mineral elements that add to those already present in the soil and

essential for plant growth.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le rôle des micro-organismes et

also calcium, magnesium, iron, and other trace elements, essential for good growth and health of the plant.

pages.title: PHOTOSYNTHESIS
pages.text:
The upper part of the plants interacts with light. The photosynthesis reaction produces sugar that will feed the

fungi and bacteria in the soil.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour PHOTOSYNTHÈSE

pages.title: In exchange for the sugar it provides, some fungi act as a mouth for the plant: they absorb soil elements on its
pages.text:
behalf. This win-win relationship is called a symbiosis. When it is established between a plant and a fungus, it is

then called mycorrhiza.

pages.text:

organic matter they bring in decomposing is therefore not negligible !

pages.title: X3
pages.text:
The technique of intensive organic gardening in living soil with permanent beds and mulching improves soil

fertility while tripling the production of vegetables compared to conventional methods.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour X3

pages.title: The cultivation bed technique has many advantages: by preserving the soil, it allows for a reduction in inputs of
pages.text: compost and organic matter, thus saving money, while increasing productivity and producing healthy food.
